arXiv:2611.26346v1 [cs.AI] 19 Nov 2026
Abstract

Managing concurrent tasks across separate agent sessions quickly exhausts human attention, motivating always-on personal agents behind a single continuous interface. Yet when every context shares identical frozen backbone weights, funneling interleaved dialogues and external events into one linear session induces cross-topic constraint bleed and head-of-line stalling. Conversely, router–ticket hierarchies incur lossy prose handoffs, heavy routing overhead, and blind merges—collapsing true-conflict repository merges to a 33.3%33.3\% three-run mean despite high isolated branch passes. Rather than scheduling anthropomorphic roles, we introduce ClonAct, a routerless architecture that virtualizes context blocks directly through a pluggable single-pass non-generative Context MMU, in-place Context Cells, a footprint-aware Synaptic Bus with an isolated trial merge gate, and a wave-flushed Shared Trunk. Across three programmatic multi-stream benchmarks and three model families, our portable trial merge gate lifts true-conflict merges to 63.3%63.3\%, while ClonAct’s routerless virtualization attains this ceiling with 45.9%45.9\% fewer prompt tokens and prevents compact-model router collapse. Under continuous surge streams, ClonAct matches top completion (95.0%95.0\%) with the lowest median wait and zero timed-out status checks.

Keywords: 
LLM Agents, Context Scheduling, Personal Agents, Multi-Agent Systems, Prefix KV-Cache

.

1 Introduction

Modern tool-using language model agents can complete a range of coding and workflow tasks end-to-end within an isolated session (Yao et al., 2023; Yang et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2025). In daily work, however, tasks rarely run one at a time: users advance multiple tasks in parallel while asynchronous requests and notifications continue arriving from external channels (Froger et al., 2026). Today, users typically isolate concurrent work by manually opening separate sessions and workspaces, yet monitoring progress, switching focus, and ferrying intermediate findings across many live sessions quickly exhausts human attention (Qiao, 2026; DeepSeek Harness Team, 2026). Building an always-on personal agent therefore requires hiding session management inside the runtime so that users interact through a single continuous interface (Packer et al., 2023; DeepSeek Harness Team, 2026)—raising a central architectural question: how should an agent system coordinate concurrent tasks behind one unified window when every underlying instance shares the same model weights?

Long-context studies document sensitivity to input length and evidence position (Liu et al., 2024; Levy et al., 2024). In our interleaved-task diagnosis (Section 2), a single linear context (DSH-Mono, Figure 1a) also exhibits cross-task constraint bleed—a read-only lookup caveat can suppress an in-flight code change—while long tool turns stall status queries by 3.9×3.9\times (Figure 2a). Moreover, as cumulative-request experiments by Qiao (2026) demonstrate, subagent delegation in a monolithic session is prompt-dependent and not guaranteed, motivating structural separation behind one entry point via multi-role teams (DSH-AgentTeam; Hong et al., 2024; Wu et al., 2024; Qian et al., 2024) or a resident top-level router that summarizes dialogues into isolated worker mandates (DSH-SuperAgent, Figure 1b; Qiao, 2026; DeepSeek Harness Team, 2026). Yet unlike human organizations whose heterogeneous expertise requires role division and verbal handoffs, agent instances sharing identical System-2 weights (θ1=θ2=θ\theta_{1}=\theta_{2}=\theta) can be scheduled to continue the same supplied context without a new prose handoff. Under a locked execution kernel (Section 2), when workloads move from independent tasks to interactive clarification and shared-repository edits, interposing role or router layers incurs three measurable costs: handoff serialization loss as static tickets drop alignment nuances (Section 4.6), a last-mile merge cliff where concurrent workers pass 90.0%90.0\% of true-conflict pairs inside isolated branches yet drop to a 33.3%33.3\% three-run mean (10.0%10.0\% in Run 1) upon merging, and up to 2.6×2.6\times prompt token volume over single-session execution from repeated router decoding.

Motivated by effective single-agent loops in existing deployments (Sarkis, 2026), we decouple cross-task multiplexing from top-down task decomposition and propose ClonAct (Figure 1c; Section 3, Figure 3), which schedules context blocks, rather than anthropomorphic roles, directly as virtualized resources. All System-2 execution and dialogue Context Cells share identical frozen weights πθ\pi_{\theta} with zero generative router layer, while a pluggable single-pass non-generative Context MMU—instantiated either with a lightweight probability-scoring classifier or same-weight single-token log-probability probing of πθ\pi_{\theta}—routes user turns and external events directly to independent Context Cells. Each cell clarifies requirements with the user in a zero-directory read-only state and, upon confirmation, promotes in-place to lazy-mounted Git worktree execution along its exact alignment token spine—avoiding ticket rewriting while retaining stable prefixes compatible with provider-side caching. Across concurrent cells, a footprint-aware Synaptic Bus blocks raw tool noise while synchronizing shared AST and resource footprints ahead of a three-stage isolated trial merge gate, atop a byte-locked Shared Trunk that grounds workspace conventions across cells.

To complement task-based coding and app benchmarks (Jimenez et al., 2024; Trivedi et al., 2024) with interleaved intake and shared-workspace concurrency, we construct three zero-overlap programmatic suites (Section 4.1): Synaptic-Bench-150, pairing live repository, database, and office sandboxes with deterministic tool-count Step-Hooks; AppWorld-Micro-30, an uncoupled everyday-errand control; and Synaptic-Stream-60, feeding continuous 240240-event omnichannel streams under moderate and 2.5×2.5\times surge arrival rates. Across 1,8001{,}800 episodic rollouts, 170170 diagnostic controls, and 3636 continuous streams over three model families, our controls separate two complementary effects: the portable trial merge gate lifts true-conflict merges from 33.3%33.3\% to 63.3%63.3\% across three runs (10.0%→80.0%10.0\%\to 80.0\% in Run 1), while ClonAct’s routerless virtualization attains this ceiling with 45.9%45.9\% fewer prompt tokens than DSH-SuperAgent, 100.0%100.0\% orchestration safety, and zero penalty on uncoupled errands. Under conflict-free surge streams, ClonAct matches top completion (95.0%95.0\%) with the lowest median wait and zero timed-out status checks, while dual-tier billing exposes explicit load-dependent cost trade-offs. Pre-registered ablations validate target-slice causal dissociation and same-weight log-probability gating, and cross-backbone runs improve pooled resolution by +11.5+11.5 pp over DSH-SuperAgent while preventing compact-model router collapse.

Our contributions are threefold:

  • •

    We propose ClonAct, a routerless architecture that schedules homogeneous System-2 Context Cells as virtualized resources via a pluggable single-pass Context MMU, in-place align-to-execute promotion, footprint-aware synaptic reconciliation, and a wave-flushed Shared Trunk (Section 3).

  • •

    We introduce Synaptic-Bench-150, AppWorld-Micro-30, and Synaptic-Stream-60, zero-overlap multi-stream benchmarks combining un-partitioned intake, deterministic Step-Hooks, live repository conflicts, and dual-rate continuous arrival streams under deterministic state oracles (Section 4.1).

  • •

    We isolate the causal roles of trial-merge settlement and routerless virtualization across three model families, resolving bleed and merge cliffs while exposing explicit dual-tier cost and backbone-floor trade-offs (Section 4).

2 Problem Formulation and Mechanism Diagnosis

Before introducing our architecture, we formalize concurrent agent orchestration over homogeneous model weights, recover existing paradigms as structural special cases, and empirically isolate why each breaks down under interleaved and state-coupled workloads.

2.1 Two-Operator Formulation of Concurrent Agents

Consider an always-on personal agent backed by a frozen black-box language model policy πθ\pi_{\theta} acting over a mutable shared workspace 𝒲t\mathcal{W}_{t} (code repositories, relational databases, filesystems, and personal applications). Rather than receiving one isolated prompt, the system observes an arrival-ordered omnichannel event stream ℰ={(et,τt,st)}t=1T\mathcal{E}=\{(e_{t},\tau_{t},s_{t})\}_{t=1}^{T} (τ1≤⋯≤τT\tau_{1}\leq\dots\leq\tau_{T}), interleaving foreground user dialogue (st=chats_{t}=\mathrm{chat}: multi-turn clarifications, mid-flight status checks, side lookups, and requirement amendments) with external channels (st=exts_{t}=\mathrm{ext}: actionable webhooks, duplicate alerts, and bystander chatter).

Any homogeneous-weight concurrent agent decomposes into (a) an upper-layer context orchestrator 𝒪\mathcal{O} and (b) the shared single-session execution kernel πθ\pi_{\theta}. At event tt, 𝒪\mathcal{O} maintains active execution contexts {𝒞k}k=1Kt\{\mathcal{C}_{k}\}_{k=1}^{K_{t}}—discrete message sequences over roles {system,user,assistant,tool}\{\mathrm{system},\mathrm{user},\mathrm{assistant},\mathrm{tool}\}—via three control operations: (i) ingress routing and sandbox promotion, mapping ete_{t} to a context 𝒞k\mathcal{C}_{k} and deciding when to mount an isolated write directory (e.g., a Git worktree); (ii) cross-context visibility, governing what state flows between sibling contexts 𝒞j↔𝒞k\mathcal{C}_{j}\leftrightarrow\mathcal{C}_{k} (j≠kj\neq k); and (iii) workspace settlement, reconciling sandbox mutations into 𝒲t\mathcal{W}_{t}. Unlike human teams where distinct roles reflect heterogeneous human expertise, every context here queries the identical distribution πθ(⋅∣𝒞k)\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid\mathcal{C}_{k}) (θ1=θ2=θ\theta_{1}=\theta_{2}=\theta): capability asymmetries arise solely from which tokens 𝒪\mathcal{O} populates inside 𝒞k\mathcal{C}_{k}.

Trivial Base Case and Paradigm Specializations. When a single task runs undisturbed (Kt=1K_{t}=1, zero mid-flight interleaving or concurrent writes), 𝒪\mathcal{O} reduces to identity pass-through to the underlying single-session harness. Under concurrent streams, existing paradigms instantiate 𝒪\mathcal{O} at opposite extremes: (1) Flat single-session (DSH-Mono; Yao et al., 2023) fixes Kt≡1K_{t}\equiv 1, appending all events into 𝒞1\mathcal{C}_{1} over one working directory; (2) Delegation-first subagent forking (DSH-Subagent-Fork; Qiao, 2026) prompts 𝒞1\mathcal{C}_{1} to spawn or prefix-fork child contexts on demand; (3) Multi-role peer teams (DSH-AgentTeam; Hong et al., 2024; Wu et al., 2024) coordinate a lead context and isolated workers via natural-language blackboards and peer mailboxes; and (4) Resident router–ticket–worker (DSH-SuperAgent; Qiao, 2026; DeepSeek Harness Team, 2026) places a persistent generative coordinator 𝒞router\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{router}} in front to filter events and summarize dialogues into isolated worker mandates.

2.2 Controlled Diagnosis of Existing Paradigms

To isolate upper-layer orchestration 𝒪\mathcal{O} free of low-level tool confounders, we lock all four existing paradigms onto the identical single-session DSH execution substrate with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 across 150150 multi-stream episodes combining interactive clarifications, mid-flight amendments, and concurrent repository/app mutations (Section 4.1). Let pθ⋆p_{\theta}^{\star} denote πθ\pi_{\theta}’s undisturbed single-task ceiling, and let plocp_{\mathrm{loc}} and pjointp_{\mathrm{joint}} denote pre-settlement local sandbox accuracy and post-settlement workspace accuracy under 𝒪\mathcal{O}. Adding and subtracting plocp_{\mathrm{loc}} decomposes the concurrent orchestration gap Δconc​(𝒪)≜pθ⋆−pjoint\Delta_{\mathrm{conc}}(\mathcal{O})\triangleq p_{\theta}^{\star}-p_{\mathrm{joint}} into two observable stages:

Δconc​(𝒪)=(pθ⋆−ploc)⏟Intra-context distortion+(ploc−pjoint)⏟Last-mile settlement gap.\Delta_{\mathrm{conc}}(\mathcal{O})=\underbrace{\bigl(p_{\theta}^{\star}-p_{\mathrm{loc}}\bigr)}_{\text{Intra-context distortion}}+\underbrace{\bigl(p_{\mathrm{loc}}-p_{\mathrm{joint}}\bigr)}_{\text{Last-mile settlement gap}}. (1)

Empirical trace forensics (Figure 2) show how existing paradigms trigger one or both terms of Equation 1:

1. Cross-Stream Constraint Bleed and Head-of-Line Stalling. In DSH-Mono (Kt≡1K_{t}\equiv 1), editing one directory serially sets ploc=pjointp_{\mathrm{loc}}=p_{\mathrm{joint}} (zero merge gap on single-domain coding, 74.5%74.5\%), yet interleaving cross-modal streams inflates intra-context distortion (54.0%54.0\% overall)—falling to 33.3%33.3\% when foreground read-only caveats (“do not modify business code”) contaminate active code edits (Figure 2b)—while active tool turns stall mid-flight status peeks for 28.3​s28.3\text{s} (Figure 2a). Prompting the main loop to spawn subagents (DSH-Subagent-Fork) alleviates office interference but neither unblocks the parent coordinator (38.2​s38.2\text{s}) nor prevents cross-modal bleed (41.7%41.7\%).

2. Authority–Information Inversion and Generative Routing Tax. In our router baseline, natural-language handoffs across identical weights (θ1=θ2=θ\theta_{1}=\theta_{2}=\theta) place routing and summarization in a top-level context without the workers’ full file and test observations. Unstructured blackboards and peer mailboxes (DSH-AgentTeam, 227227 teammate sessions) degrade accuracy below DSH-Mono (60.0%60.0\% overall, 42.0​s42.0\text{s} peek stall). While a resident generative router (DSH-SuperAgent) unblocks status peeks (11.9​s11.9\text{s}) and external intake, autoregressive router decoding on every event inflates episode tokens by 2.6×2.6\times (6.36​M6.36\text{M} vs. 2.44​M2.44\text{M}; 426.3​s426.3\text{s} wall-clock), over-rejects 23.3%23.3\% of everyday non-repository errands, and induces severe ticket-paraphrasing loss (S~k=πθrouter​(Sk)\tilde{S}_{k}=\pi_{\theta}^{\mathrm{router}}(S_{k})) in the first term of Equation 1 when backbone capacity tightens (Section 4.5).

3. Sibling Sandbox Blindness and the Last-Mile Merge Cliff. Crucially, isolating concurrent workers inside blind Git worktrees (DSH-SuperAgent, originally designed for independent per-ticket branches; DeepSeek Harness Team, 2026) succeeds on a counterfactual control where concurrent features edit disjoint symbols (80.0%80.0\% post-merge pass rate, Figure 2b). Yet when concurrent features touch overlapping symbols, workers still achieve ploc=90.0%p_{\mathrm{loc}}=90.0\% (9/109/10, matching the undisturbed single-task ceiling pθ⋆=90.0%p_{\theta}^{\star}=90.0\%; Section 4.2) inside isolated branches, only to collapse to a 33.3%33.3\% three-run mean (10.0%10.0\%, 1/101/10 in Run 1) upon sequential git merge onto the main branch—a 56.756.7 pp three-run mean (80.080.0 pp Run-1) settlement gap in Equation 1 that reflects blind worktree isolation without pre-merge semantic reconciliation as the second merge overwrites or collides with sibling signatures.

2.3 Design Principles for Context Scheduling

Existing paradigms trade one term of Equation 1 for the other: single-session execution eliminates merge gaps at the cost of cross-stream bleed and blocking, whereas role and router hierarchies buy isolation through lossy prose handoffs, 2.6×2.6\times routing overhead, and blind merges. Driving both terms toward zero requires scheduling context blocks directly under four design principles: (i) sub-second non-generative multiplexing (Section 3.1), removing autoregressive decoding from per-event ingress routing; (ii) same-brain trajectory continuity (Section 3.2), promoting interactive alignment into isolated execution along one continuous token spine without ticket rewriting; (iii) footprint-aware pre-merge reconciliation (Section 3.3), isolating raw tool noise while synchronizing shared symbol footprints and trial-testing joint merges before updating the main branch; and (iv) prefix-locked workspace grounding (Section 3.4), sharing verified workspace conventions across virtualized contexts behind a byte-identical left prefix updated only at idle wave boundaries.

3 Context as a Resource: The ClonAct Architecture

To realize these four principles over homogeneous weights πθ\pi_{\theta}, ClonAct removes the generative middleman router and schedules context blocks directly as virtualized resources behind one continuous interface (Figure 3). At wave epoch e∈ℕe\in\mathbb{N}, active and parked Context Cells {𝒞k}k=1Kt\{\mathcal{C}_{k}\}_{k=1}^{K_{t}} follow a left-locked layout:

𝒞k=T0(e)⏟Byte-0 prefix⊕Sk⏟Intent spine⊕Hk⏟Scratchpad,\mathcal{C}_{k}\;=\;\underbrace{\;T_{0}^{(e)}\;}_{\text{Byte-0 prefix}}\;\oplus\;\underbrace{\;\;S_{k}\;\;}_{\text{Intent spine}}\;\oplus\;\underbrace{\;\;H_{k}\;\;}_{\text{Scratchpad}}, (2)

concatenating a byte-identical Shared Trunk T0(e)T_{0}^{(e)} at byte 00, a monotonic Intent Spine SkS_{k} hosting direct user turns, and an evolving Tool Scratchpad HkH_{k} (complete pseudocode in Appendix A, Algorithm 1).

3.1 Single-Pass Ingress Multiplexing (Context MMU)

To eliminate autoregressive latency at ingress, the Context MMU evaluates parallel single-pass binary and categorical probability-scoring classifiers over a compact runtime state Ωt=(𝒫ws,{Φk}k=1Kt)\Omega_{t}=(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{ws}},\{\Phi_{k}\}_{k=1}^{K_{t}}). Here 𝒫ws\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{ws}} summarizes workspace conventions and Φk=(σk,Φkread,Φkwrite,Φkdom,mk)\Phi_{k}=(\sigma_{k},\Phi_{k}^{\mathrm{read}},\Phi_{k}^{\mathrm{write}},\Phi_{k}^{\mathrm{dom}},m_{k}) tracks cell lifecycle state σk\sigma_{k}, touched AST symbols/files, CLI/filesystem domains, and latest verified milestone mkm_{k}. Without generating chain-of-thought or JSON tokens, one parallel forward pass evaluates four probabilistic gates:

  • •

    Grounded Noise Filtering & Dedup: On st=exts_{t}=\mathrm{ext}, actionability score pact​(et∣Ωt)∈[0,1]p_{\mathrm{act}}(e_{t}\mid\Omega_{t})\in[0,1] drops bystander chatter and merges duplicate alerts into active 𝒞k∗\mathcal{C}_{k^{*}} without redundant spawns.

  • •

    Three-Way Intent Granularity: Foreground turns (st=chats_{t}=\mathrm{chat}) classify over gint∈{atomic,seq,par}g_{\mathrm{int}}\in\{\mathrm{atomic},\mathrm{seq},\mathrm{par}\}. Only gint=parg_{\mathrm{int}}=\mathrm{par} (orthogonal multi-intent) invokes a one-shot, tool-free clause rewrite by the System-2 backbone πθ\pi_{\theta} (accounted in total billed tokens) to resolve elided pronouns across parallel cells, falling back to single-cell sequential execution under shared-state ordering.

  • •

    Lifecycle Coreference & Caveat Isolation: An LRU-bounded window of up to KmaxK_{\max} active and recently settled cells remains addressable in Ωt\Omega_{t} (demoting older summaries to L3L_{3}) so follow-ups wake 𝒞k∗\mathcal{C}_{k^{*}} in place. Routing isolates foreground read-only caveats from active background cells and requests a one-line disambiguation whenever maxk⁡P⁡(k∣et,Ωt)<τconf\max_{k}P(k\mid e_{t},\Omega_{t})<\tau_{\mathrm{conf}}.

  • •

    Non-Blocking Peeks & Zero-Dir Observers: Because stateless MMU routing decouples control-plane queries from active worker tool loops, a status check on an in-flight cell 𝒞k∗\mathcal{C}_{k^{*}} avoids blocking or steering the worker by issuing an out-of-band, tool-free System-2 summary call reusing pinned prefix T0(e)T_{0}^{(e)} plus a compact live state slice of 𝒞k∗\mathcal{C}_{k^{*}}’s progress and audit trail. Derived requests conditioned on in-flight work spawn a zero-worktree Observer Cell (σk=obs\sigma_{k}=\mathrm{obs}) subscribed to 𝒞k∗\mathcal{C}_{k^{*}} via the Synaptic Bus.

3.2 Same-Brain Context Cells and In-Place Promotion

To preserve alignment context without prose handoffs, each task runs from clarification to delivery inside the same cell 𝒞k\mathcal{C}_{k} (Figure 3b). Ambiguous prompts or standalone lookups enter σk=align\sigma_{k}=\mathrm{align} with zero Git worktree allocation: rather than altering tool schemas inside T0(e)T_{0}^{(e)} (which would invalidate prefix KV-caches), write isolation is enforced at the local tool executor via guard ℳro\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ro}}. Pure lookups settle and archive here, while topic switches park 𝒞k\mathcal{C}_{k} (σk=parked\sigma_{k}=\mathrm{parked}) at zero compute. Upon user confirmation (σk:align↦exec\sigma_{k}:\mathrm{align}\mapsto\mathrm{exec}), 𝒞k\mathcal{C}_{k} lazily mounts an isolated Git worktree, lifts ℳro\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ro}}, and continues in-place directly from T0(e)⊕SkT_{0}^{(e)}\oplus S_{k} in Equation 2 with zero prose ticket rewriting, applying watermark compaction strictly inside HkH_{k} while keeping T0(e)⊕SkT_{0}^{(e)}\oplus S_{k} pinned.

3.3 Hybrid Synaptic Bus and Three-Stage Settlement

While worktrees isolate raw tool output, the Synaptic Bus synchronizes shared state across two horizontal tiers and a settlement gate. During execution, deterministic static AST symbol and CLI/domain extraction (Tier 0, zero LLM tokens) updates Φkread,Φkwrite\Phi_{k}^{\mathrm{read}},\Phi_{k}^{\mathrm{write}}; touching Φjwrite\Phi_{j}^{\mathrm{write}} (j≠kj\neq k) emits a non-blocking alert prompting read-only peek_peer_cell(𝒞j)(\mathcal{C}_{j}) inspection, plus trunk-advance notices when siblings merge. At cross-modal milestones (Tier 1), probabilistic conductance pk→j∈[0,1]p_{k\to j}\in[0,1] tail-appends verified deltas guarded by a directed refractory ledger ℛsyn\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{syn}}, while goal overturns abort and roll back cleanly. Before updating the main branch, 𝒞k\mathcal{C}_{k} runs an isolated trial merge inside its own worktree (Figure 3b): (a) Orthogonal Fast-Track promotes conflict-free, disjoint-footprint commits at zero LLM cost; (b) Conflict Reconciliation mounts sibling intent and diff slices to resolve markers and pass unit tests before touching the main branch; and (c) Semantic Joint Gate runs joint regression tests whenever clean line merges touch shared symbols.

Proposition 3.1 (Runtime Invariants of ClonAct).

Under Algorithm 1, within wave ee: (i) Prefix Byte Identity: all active cells share byte-identical prefix T0(e)T_{0}^{(e)} and union schema UtoolsU_{\mathrm{tools}}; (ii) Executor Tool-API Read-Only Guard: whenever ContextMMU assigns a turn to σk∈{align,obs}\sigma_{k}\in\{\mathrm{align},\mathrm{obs}\}, no Git worktree is mounted, mutating and delegation tool APIs (write, edit, subagent, send_message) are deterministically denied at executor plugin ℳro\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ro}}, and bash is disabled during non-inspection alignment; (iii) Acyclic Broadcast Termination: given a bounded per-cell milestone budget MmaxM_{\max}, ℛsyn\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{syn}} guarantees cycle-free, finite milestone propagation (at most Mmax​Kt​(Kt−1)M_{\max}K_{t}(K_{t}-1) deliveries); and (iv) Single-Task Reduction: for Kt=1K_{t}=1 with an undisturbed task, conditioned on single-cell ingress routing, ClonAct reduces prompt construction to the underlying single-session harness without middleman summarization loss (verification in Appendix A).

Security Scope. While Proposition 3.1(ii) deterministically enforces read-only tool-API gating at the executor layer, strict kernel-level zero-mutation guarantees against arbitrary shell side effects during read-only workspace inspection rely on OS-level read-only filesystem sandboxing (e.g., a read-only macOS Seatbelt profile).

Control-Plane Complexity. Equation 3 characterizes raw input-token scaling rather than direct API billing: when provider prefix caches absorb ∼98%\sim\!98\% of router replay at heavily discounted cached-read rates, router dollar spend grows more slowly than raw token volume, whereas stateless uncached System-1 calls pay higher per-token input pricing—a dual-tier trade-off analyzed directly in Section 4.3 and Appendix C. Tier-0 AST/domain tracking, peek_peer_cell, and Path A orthogonal merges incur zero LLM tokens.

Implementation. Every cell runs unmodified DSH (@deepseek-ai/dsh v0.2.1-rc.3) with Seatbelt sandboxing and automatic watermark compaction. Without per-model retuning (τconf=0.55\tau_{\mathrm{conf}}=0.55, |L2|≤12|L_{2}|\leq 12), single-pass classifiers are instantiated via TypeSafe Jev (TypeSafe, n.d.) or a same-weight single-token log-probability fallback on πθ\pi_{\theta} (max_tokens=1, logprobs=True; details in Appendix C), evaluated on DeepSeek-V4.1 in Section 4.4.

4 Experiments and Mechanistic Analysis

Across 1,8001{,}800 paired episodes, 170170 supplementary diagnostic control and oracle rollouts, 3636 continuous 240240-event streams (720720 live task deliveries, 8,6408{,}640 routed events), and 150150 inner-kernel controls with zero runner errors or contamination, we test four hypotheses linking Section 2 and Section 3: (i) virtualizing context blocks without a generative router resolves the bleed-versus-merge dilemma with lower prompt-token expenditure while imposing zero penalty on uncoupled errands; (ii) under continuous conflict-free wall-clock arrivals, congestion triggers a queueing phase transition where ClonAct sustains low median wait and high verified completion without sacrificing real-time status observability; (iii) ClonAct’s four scheduling primitives exhibit orthogonal causal dissociation on their predicted target slices; and (iv) offloading ingress gating and eliminating prose ticket serialization transfers across model families and prevents compact-model router collapse.

4.1 Multi-Stream Benchmarks and Evaluation Protocol

SWE-bench and AppWorld evaluate coding and app tasks (Jimenez et al., 2024; Trivedi et al., 2024), while τ\tau-bench explicitly models dynamic tool–agent–user interaction (Yao et al., 2025). To study interleaved tasks and shared-workspace concurrency, we build three zero-overlap programmatic suites (Appendix B) graded strictly by deterministic state assertions:

  • •

    Synaptic-Bench-150 (Bench-150; N=150N=150; 161161 Tier-1, 252252 Tier-2): Mounts live repos, SQL databases, and app sandboxes from SWE-bench Verified (Chowdhury et al., 2024), SWE-Interact (Raghavendra et al., 2026), Ambig-SWE (Vijayvargiya et al., 2025), CooperBench (Khatua et al., 2026), Gaia2 (Froger et al., 2026), and MCPMark (Wu et al., 2025b) across Office (4545), Coding (5555), and Hybrid (5050) (1010 tracks): (i) interactive alignment & lookups (O-1, C-1, H-1: A→B→AA\to B\to A turns); (ii) async bursts & Step-Hooks (O-2, O-3, C-3, H-2: 150150 noise/dup events plus mid-flight amendments at exact tool-step counts); and (iii) coupled concurrency (C-2: 1010 true-conflict and 1010 disjoint repo pairs; H-3: cross-modal observer briefs; H-4: 33-wave evolution).

  • •

    AppWorld-Micro-30 (Micro-30; N=30N=30; 6060-errand TGC, 100100 verifiers): Pairs app-disjoint errands (Δ​DBA∩Δ​DBB=∅\Delta\mathrm{DB}_{A}\cap\Delta\mathrm{DB}_{B}=\emptyset; M-1..3) from AppWorld (Trivedi et al., 2024) with 7070 chatter and 3030 duplicate alerts as a zero-coupling control.

  • •

    Synaptic-Stream-60 (Stream-60; 33 streams, 6060 unique tasks, 240240 events/stream): Extends the cumulative-arrival design of Qiao (2026) from mock slow tools to three conflict-free heterogeneous streams mounting persistent 33-project Git monorepos (Click, Jinja2, DSPy, NetworkX; 0%0\% intra-stream file overlap by construction) and 1717-persona multi-account AppWorld sandboxes with zero feature, SWE-instance, or AppWorld task/generator overlap against Bench-150 and Micro-30. Each stream injects 2020 tasks (33 disjoint coding features, 1111 multi-step app writes, 66 read-only lookups) interleaved with 22 directly tested spec amendments (+18​s+18\text{s}/+7.2​s+7.2\text{s}), 178178 unmentioned group messages, 2424 colleague reposts, and 1616 untagged status checks under Moderate (∼30​s\sim\!30\text{s}/request) and 2.5×2.5\times Surge (∼12​s\sim\!12\text{s}/request) arrival rates across six paradigms (adding DSH-Subagent-Neutral without delegation-first prompting).

Kernel Parity and Stratified Protocol. All arms execute unmodified DSH over identical unfiltered streams and receive the identical workspace conventions block (Appendix C)—with DSH-SuperAgent running the official open-source prototype (DeepSeek Harness Team, 2026; pinned commit in Appendix C) under symmetric allowlists—summing billed prompt/cache tokens from DSH telemetry plus MMU calls. Ablations and multi-model runs pair Micro-30 with Bench-60, a pre-registered 40.0%40.0\% stratified subset of Bench-150 selected by deterministic SHA-256 episode hashing (1818 Office, 2222 Coding with all 1010 true-conflict C-2 pairs plus 22 disjoint pairs, 2020 Hybrid; Appendix D), reporting raw rates and Horvitz–Thompson IPW estimates (N^=150\hat{N}=150; Horvitz & Thompson, 1952) across DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, Qwen3.8-Flash, and GPT-6-Luna.

4.2 Resolving the Concurrency Dilemma

ClonAct eliminates cross-stream bleed and merge cliffs without router overhead. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (Table 1; per-track splits in Appendix E), ClonAct reaches 74.7%74.7\% (112/150112/150) and is the sole paradigm achieving 100.0%100.0\% (161/161161/161) Tier-1 safety, significantly beating DSH-Mono (66.0%66.0\%, p=0.0294p=0.0294) and DSH-AgentTeam (60.0%60.0\%, p=0.0007p=0.0007). DSH-Mono ties ClonAct on Coding (74.5%74.5\%) via single-directory edits, yet cross-modal bleed drops its Hybrid accuracy to 54.0%54.0\% (H-3: 33.3%33.3\% vs. 91.7%91.7\%) and stalls peeks by 3.9×3.9\times (28.3​s28.3\text{s} vs. 7.3​s7.3\text{s}). On full Bench-150, ClonAct leads DSH-SuperAgent (72.0%72.0\%) by +2.7+2.7 pp (+18/−14+18/-14, two-sided McNemar p=0.60p=0.60), with non-conflicting single-ticket tracks forming the majority of the denominator while coupled concurrency drives sharp separation—lifting Run-1 true-conflict C-2 merges from 10.0%10.0\% (1/101/10) to 80.0%80.0\% (8/108/10, +7/−0+7/-0, p=0.0156p=0.0156) and H-3 cross-modal briefs from 66.7%66.7\% to 91.7%91.7\%—while cutting prompt tokens by 45.9%45.9\% (510.6510.6M vs. 943.7943.7M), worktrees by 49.8%49.8\% (148148 vs. 295295), and total dual-tier USD spend by 38.9%38.9\% ($6.92 vs. $11.33; Appendix C, Table 9). On multi-turn office tracks (O-1/O-3; Appendix E, Table 11), explicit read-only alignment occasionally leads the backbone to under-execute writes after confirmation while maintaining 100.0%100.0\% Tier-1 safety; on the 1010-episode C-2 Disjoint control, ClonAct passes 6/106/10 (60.0%60.0\%) vs. DSH-SuperAgent’s 8/108/10 (80.0%80.0\%), comprising two shared backbone failures plus two single-test edge misses under clean merges (per-episode audit in Appendix F). Consistent with Equation 3, 1,2961{,}296 single-pass MMU calls average 0.55​s0.55\text{s}/call and 0.56%0.56\% of prompt tokens (2.86​M2.86\text{M}, $0.12 across all 150150 episodes) while System-2 workers sustain a 97.9%97.9\% prefix cache hit rate.

Zero coordination penalty on uncoupled errands, multiplicative with inner-kernel quality. Confirming Proposition 3.1(iv) on app-disjoint Micro-30 (Table 1, right), ClonAct (90.0%90.0\%, 27/3027/30) matches DSH-Mono (93.3%93.3\%, 28/3028/30, p=1.00p=1.00), whereas DSH-SuperAgent drops to 76.7%76.7\% with 2.3×2.3\times higher token volume. Conversely, replacing ClonAct’s inner DSH loop with a minimal Python loop on Synaptic-Bench-150 (Appendix E) retains 60.0%60.0\% true-conflict merges and 7.0​s7.0\text{s} peeks but lowers overall pass rate to 57.3%57.3\% (−17.3-17.3 pp), showing that ClonAct amplifies mature single-session harnesses. Because isolated short episodes reset workspaces between runs and include turn-settlement barriers, Table 1 omits episodic wall-clock drain time—which cannot capture cross-task queueing under continuous arrivals—and we evaluate streaming latency directly below.

Portable trial-merge settlement vs. routerless architectural efficiency. To separate our settlement gate from router elimination on Track C-2 (N=20N=20; Table 2a, Trial Merge path forensics in Appendix E), we upgrade unmodified DSH-SuperAgent solely with ClonAct’s Three-Stage Trial Merge Gate (DSH-SuperAgent + Trial Merge). This lifts its true-conflict merge rate from 10.0%10.0\% to 80.0%80.0\% (+70.0+70.0 pp, exact two-sided McNemar p=0.0156p=0.0156) with exact 20/2020/20 pass concordance against ClonAct (70.0%70.0\% all, 60.0%60.0\% disjoint). Thus, the portable trial merge gate drives the merge-accuracy ceiling, whereas attaining that ceiling atop a generative router and blind worktrees costs 12.97​M12.97\text{M} tokens/ep, $2.733 total (including $0.259 and +121.5​s+121.5\text{s}/ep of post-hoc reconciliation across 19/2019/20 episodes), 549.0​s549.0\text{s}/ep wall-clock, and 96.7%96.7\% Tier-1 safety (one episode’s tasks dropped silently by the router). ClonAct’s routerless virtualization attains the identical 70.0%/80.0%70.0\%/80.0\% accuracy with 51.2%51.2\% fewer tokens (6.33​M6.33\text{M}), 45.5%45.5\% lower dual-tier USD spend ($1.489, including Jev), 32.5%32.5\% faster wall-clock (370.7​s370.7\text{s}), 32.1%32.1\% faster peeks (9.4​s9.4\text{s} vs. 13.8​s13.8\text{s}), and 100.0%100.0\% (30/3030/30) safety.

Multi-run stability and empirical Equation 1 grounding. Across three independent runs on C-2 True-Conflict (3×10=303\times 10=30 paired trials/arm; Table 2b and Appendix E, Table 12), ClonAct achieves 80.0%/50.0%/60.0%80.0\%/50.0\%/60.0\% (63.3%±15.3%63.3\%\pm 15.3\% SD, 19/3019/30 pooled), outperforming DSH-SuperAgent’s 10.0%/40.0%/50.0%10.0\%/40.0\%/50.0\% (33.3%±20.8%33.3\%\pm 20.8\% SD, 10/3010/30 pooled) in all 3/33/3 runs for a +30.0+30.0 pp mean lift (1.9×1.9\times) at 38.3%38.3\% lower estimated API cost and 18.2%18.2\% faster wall-clock (378.6​s378.6\text{s} vs. 463.0​s463.0\text{s}). Accounting for episode-level clustering across N=10N=10 distinct pairs yields an exact two-sided sign-flip p=0.156p=0.156 (paired tt-test p=0.108p=0.108), reflecting limited cluster power at N=10N=10 alongside consistent 3/33/3 run wins. Running all 2020 true-conflict features undisturbed via DSH-Mono establishes an empirical ceiling of 18/2018/20 (90.0%90.0\%) features and pθ⋆=9/10p_{\theta}^{\star}=9/10 (90.0%90.0\%) pairs (only one pair fails undisturbed). Substituting pθ⋆=90.0%p_{\theta}^{\star}=90.0\% into Equation 1 validates our diagnosis: DSH-Mono incurs 20.020.0 pp intra-context distortion and 0.00.0 pp settlement gap; DSH-SuperAgent incurs 0.00.0 pp distortion (ploc=90.0%±0.0%p_{\mathrm{loc}}=90.0\%\pm 0.0\%) but a 56.756.7 pp 33-run mean (80.080.0 pp Run 1) settlement gap; and ClonAct holds distortion near zero (3.33.3 pp 33-run mean; 0.00.0 pp Run 1) while cutting the settlement gap by 58.8%58.8\% across 33 runs (23.323.3 pp; 87.5%87.5\% in Run 1, 10.010.0 pp).

4.3 Continuous Arrival Streams and Load Phase Transition

To jointly evaluate verified throughput and arrival-to-completion waiting time Wi=tstable,i−tarrive,iW_{i}=t_{\mathrm{stable},i}-t_{\mathrm{arrive},i} (setting Wi≜∞W_{i}\triangleq\infty for unverified tasks with verifiedi=0\mathrm{verified}_{i}=0) without survivor bias from unresolved tasks, we track the verified completion curve V(u)≜1N∑i=1N𝕀[Wi≤u∧verifiedi]V(u)\triangleq\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\mathbb{I}[W_{i}\leq u\land\mathrm{verified}_{i}] up to deadline τ=600​s\tau=600\text{s} and compute its upper-tail integral, the restricted mean waiting time RMWτ​(𝒪)=1N​∑i=1Nmin⁡(Wi,τ)=∫0τ(1−V⁡(u))​𝑑u\mathrm{RMW}_{\tau}(\mathcal{O})=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\min(W_{i},\tau)=\int_{0}^{\tau}(1-V(u))\,du.

Queueing phase transition and voluntary-delegation starvation. Comparing sparse Moderate (∼30​s\sim\!30\text{s}/req, Figure 4a) against 2.5×2.5\times Surge (∼12​s\sim\!12\text{s}/req, Figure 4b) streams reveals a sharp queueing phase transition cleanly decoupled from code merge conflicts (full dual-regime metrics and per-stream splits in Appendix E, Table 14–15). Under sparse Moderate traffic, queueing stays mild and DSH-Subagent-Neutral achieves the lowest RMW600\mathrm{RMW}_{600} (72.0​s72.0\text{s} vs. ClonAct’s 89.3​s89.3\text{s}, paired block CI [−35.9,0.4]​s[-35.9,0.4]\text{s}; both tied at 96.7%96.7\% completion) by running short errands inline without spawning worktrees, albeit censoring 37/4837/48 status peeks. Under 2.5×2.5\times Surge, however, single-server saturation triggers collapse: DSH-Mono’s median wait blows up 4.1×4.1\times (45.7​s→187.6​s45.7\text{s}\to 187.6\text{s}), and DSH-Subagent-Neutral drops from 96.7%96.7\% to 66.7%66.7\% (RMW600=297.8​s\mathrm{RMW}_{600}=297.8\text{s}). Trace forensics expose voluntary-delegation starvation: on S-3, DSH-Subagent-Neutral’s main session enters a 737.5​s737.5\text{s} single-turn coding loop that completes all 33 code tasks while starving all 1717 concurrent AppWorld errands (3/203/20 verified). In contrast, ClonAct ties DSH-AgentTeam at top Surge completion (95.0%95.0\%, 57/6057/60) and leads every aggregate Surge speed metric (RMW600=119.4​s\mathrm{RMW}_{600}=119.4\text{s}, p50=53.6​sp_{50}=53.6\text{s}, V⁡(60​s)=50.0%V(60\text{s})=50.0\%), reducing RMW600\mathrm{RMW}_{600} on 3/33/3 streams against DSH-Subagent-Neutral (−178.4​s-178.4\text{s}), DSH-Mono (−103.1​s-103.1\text{s}), and DSH-Subagent-Fork (−53.4​s-53.4\text{s}; all 95%95\% block and stream-cluster CIs excluding 00). Against multi-worker baselines DSH-AgentTeam (+9.0​s+9.0\text{s}, p=0.61p=0.61) and DSH-SuperAgent (+23.3​s+23.3\text{s}, block CI [−12.2,56.3]​s[-12.2,56.3]\text{s}), ClonAct’s Surge RMW600\mathrm{RMW}_{600} lead is directional across S=3S=3 streams (statistical inference details in Appendix D), while ClonAct leads cleanly on median wait (53.6​s53.6\text{s} vs. 79.6​s79.6\text{s}–87.9​s87.9\text{s}), mid-flight amendments (12/1212/12), and zero-timeout observability (96/9696/96).

Inverse load–token scaling and dual-tier API cost trade-off. Removing Git merge conflicts exposes a striking inverse load–token paradox in DSH-SuperAgent (1616 workers): despite identical event counts, DSH-SuperAgent consumes 59%59\% more tokens under sparse Moderate traffic than under Surge (79.4​M79.4\text{M} vs. 50.0​M50.0\text{M}/stream). Session forensics validate Equation 3’s Θ⁡(T2)\Theta(T^{2}) pre-compaction router scaling directly: spaced Moderate arrivals trigger 94.394.3 stateful orchestrator turns/stream (36.9​M36.9\text{M} router tokens, 46.4%46.4\% of total), whereas dense Surge bursts coalesce into 11.711.7 batched inbox turns (13.8​M13.8\text{M}, 27.7%27.7\%). By contrast, ClonAct’s stateless Context MMU remains load-invariant (301301–303303 calls, 2.80​M2.80\text{M}–2.95​M2.95\text{M} System-1 tokens) while preserving 96.9%96.9\%–97.5%97.5\% System-2 worker prefix caching, cutting total prompt tokens by 45.1%45.1\% (Surge) to 71.7%71.7\% (Moderate) and lowering Surge median wait by 26.0​s26.0\text{s} (53.6​s53.6\text{s} vs. 79.6​s79.6\text{s}). At the same time, dual-tier USD billing (Appendix C, Table 9) highlights a concrete pricing asymmetry: on Moderate streams, ClonAct cuts total API spend by 24.6%24.6\% ($0.494 vs. $0.655/stream), whereas on Surge streams total spend reaches near-parity ($0.545 vs. $0.528/stream, and exceeds DSH-AgentTeam’s $0.319) despite 45.1%45.1\% fewer tokens than DSH-SuperAgent, because 301301 uncached Jev ingress calls across 240240 events cost $0.118/stream ($0.042/1M flat) while DSH-SuperAgent’s batched router replay absorbs 98.2%98.2\% prefix-cache hits at $0.003/1M.

Short-errand responsiveness, mid-flight amendments, and observability. Category splits show why virtualized cells excel even without file overlap: under Surge, ClonAct achieves 41.8​s41.8\text{s} read-only QA and 51.9​s51.9\text{s} AppWrite median waits (1.9×1.9\times–4.4×4.4\times faster than DSH-AgentTeam, DSH-SuperAgent, and DSH-Mono) and is the sole paradigm passing all 12/1212/12 (100.0%100.0\%) mid-flight specification amendments across both regimes (every multi-agent baseline drops 11–22). Across all 9696 untagged status checks (4848/regime), decoupling control-plane peeks from both worker tool loops and resident-router queues enables ClonAct’s stateless MMU to deliver 96/9696/96 uncensored responses (7.3​s7.3\text{s} Moderate, 9.2​s9.2\text{s} Surge), whereas DSH-SuperAgent achieves fast replies when idle (4.8​s4.8\text{s} Moderate, 5.9​s5.9\text{s} Surge) yet still times out on 7/967/96 checks when its resident router is busy (44/4844/48 and 45/4845/48), and non-router loops stall 68.8%68.8\%–95.8%95.8\% of Surge peeks behind active turns (including DSH-AgentTeam, which ties ClonAct at 95.0%95.0\% Surge completion at lower USD cost while lagging by +34.2​s+34.2\text{s} in median wait and stalling 33/4833/48 peeks).

Explicit isolation trade-offs on conflict-free code. Disaggregating the 33 disjoint coding tasks per stream also clarifies an architectural latency trade-off: in-place runners (DSH-Mono 146.2​s146.2\text{s}, DSH-Subagent-Fork 151.9​s151.9\text{s}, zero worktrees) surface passing edits on main earlier than worktree-isolated arms (ClonAct 248.8​s248.8\text{s}, DSH-AgentTeam 258.8​s258.8\text{s}, DSH-SuperAgent 302.0​s302.0\text{s}), which defer main-branch visibility until verified commit promotion. Worktree isolation thus trades ∼95​s\sim\!95\text{s} of branch-promotion latency on conflict-free code for zero unrecovered regressions and the 80.0%80.0\% vs. 10.0%10.0\% merge safety shown on Bench-150. Meanwhile, ClonAct eliminates worktrees on all read-only lookups (14.014.0 vs. DSH-SuperAgent’s 20.020.0), and extending lazy mounting to skip Git worktrees for pure app-API writes (1111/stream) is a direct systems optimization.

4.4 Target-Slice Causal Dissociation

Single-variable ablations (Table 3, Figure 5a) selectively break each target mechanism on Bench-60 while leaving uncoupled Micro-30 statistically invariant (80.0%80.0\%–100.0%100.0\%, p≥0.25p\geq 0.25 vs. Full; removing components trims token overhead on simple single-wave errands without significant accuracy loss, confirming that ClonAct’s gains materialize specifically under coupled concurrency):

  • •

    Single-Pass System-1 Judge: Replacing the full probability-scoring System-1 judge (ingress MMU, Tier-1 synaptic conductance, and L3 recall jointly) with generative JSON decoding (w/ Generative Judge) drops Bench-60 IPW accuracy by 8.28.2 pp (one-sided p=0.029p=0.029), slows peeks by 29.3%29.3\% (8.6​s→11.1​s8.6\text{s}\to 11.1\text{s}), and sharply degrades cross-cell/multi-wave tracks (C-2: 83.3%→41.7%83.3\%\to 41.7\%, true conflicts 80.0%→30.0%80.0\%\to 30.0\%; H-4 3-wave evolution: 66.7%→0.0%66.7\%\to 0.0\%). Trace logs show that all seven C-2 failures still route concurrent features to distinct cells at ingress but fail final merged verification under noisy downstream conductance and L3 recall, whereas uncoupled Micro-30 errands remain unaffected (100.0%100.0\%).

  • •

    Same-Brain Continuity: Cold ticket handoffs (w/o Same-Brain) cause the steepest IPW drop (−17.3-17.3 pp, one-sided p=0.026p=0.026), cutting handoff episodes (N=22N=22) from 77.3%77.3\% to 54.5%54.5\% and C-1+O-1 from 81.8%81.8\% to 27.3%27.3\% (one-sided p=0.035p=0.035).

  • •

    Synaptic Bus & Settlement: Removing Synapse (Tier-0 AST peeking and the Three-Stage Trial Merge Gate jointly) leaves Office intact (83.3%→83.3%83.3\%\to 83.3\%) while collapsing C-2 merges from 83.3%83.3\% to 16.7%16.7\% (+8/−0+8/-0, two-sided p=0.0078p=0.0078; true conflicts 80.0%→10.0%80.0\%\to 10.0\%). Combined with the Track C-2 crossover control (Table 2a), these results isolate the trial merge gate as the primary driver of merge accuracy while suggesting that live footprint awareness further trims post-hoc reconciliation overhead.

  • •

    Shared Trunk & Grounding: Stripping workspace grounding and wave-flushed retention lowers IPW accuracy by 10.010.0 pp (O-1+H-2: 66.7%→33.3%66.7\%\to 33.3\%) and slows completion to 341.5​s341.5\text{s} (+16.2%+16.2\%).

Same-weight log-probability gating control. To verify that single-pass gating does not depend on an external classifier, w/ Logprob-MMU (Table 3) routes all 671/671671/671 System-1 calls (487487 Bench-60 + 184184 Micro-30) via single-token log-probability probing of πθ\pi_{\theta} (00 TypeSafe Jev calls; mean 0.97​s0.97\text{s}/call on Bench-60, 0.74​s0.74\text{s}/call on Micro-30). On Bench-60, it reaches 81.7%81.7\% raw (49/6049/60) and 83.7%83.7\% IPW—matching Jev (+1+1 net, two-sided p=1.00p=1.00) while beating w/ Generative Judge (+9+9 net, one-sided p=0.0318p=0.0318, two-sided p=0.064p=0.064) at 272.8​s272.8\text{s} wall, 5.3​s5.3\text{s} peeks, 98.5%98.5\% Tier-1 safety (67/6867/68), 98.1%98.1\% S2 cache hit, and $3.12 total off-peak USD ($0.052/ep). On short-horizon Micro-30, w/ Logprob-MMU scores 80.0%80.0\% vs. 90.0%90.0\% (p=0.38p=0.38), with the gap concentrated in M-2 read-to-write transitions (60.0%60.0\% vs. 90.0%90.0\%) while preserving 100.0%100.0\% RO safety and hygiene. Thus, on DeepSeek-V4.1, single-pass probability gating preserves multi-stream Bench-60 gains without external System-1 dependencies, with room to refine fine-grained read–write transitions.

4.5 Cross-Backbone Generalization and Router Collapse

Cross-backbone generalization and router-collapse prevention. Pooled across all three backbones (N=270N=270/arm; Table 4, Figure 5b), ClonAct leads both Combined-90 episode (63.0%63.0\%, 170/270170/270) and verifier (84.7%84.7\%, 701/828701/828) resolution—beating DSH-SuperAgent by +11.5+11.5 pp (5454W/2323L, p=0.0005p=0.0005) with 43.6%43.6\% fewer Bench-60 tokens, while beating DSH-Mono on Combined-90 episodes (63.0%63.0\% vs. 59.6%59.6\%) and verifiers (84.7%84.7\% vs. 79.8%79.8\%) and speeding up mid-flight peeks by 4.5×4.5\times–5.9×5.9\times. Transparently, on Bench-60 IPW alone, DSH-Mono edges out ClonAct on Qwen3.8-Flash (55.6%55.6\% vs. 45.8%45.8\%), GPT-6-Luna (53.7%53.7\% vs. 48.7%48.7\%), and Pooled IPW (60.7%60.7\% vs. 58.7%58.7\%); however, DSH-Mono achieves this by serializing all tasks in one directory at the cost of severe 38.5​s38.5\text{s}–67.0​s67.0\text{s} peek stalls, cross-modal bleed (H-3: 40.0%40.0\%–60.0%60.0\% vs. ClonAct’s 80.0%80.0\%–100.0%100.0\%), and lower Micro-30 pass rates (64.4%64.4\% vs. 73.3%73.3\%).

Offloading ingress gating and eliminating prose tickets prevent compact-model router collapse. While DeepSeek-V4.1 partially absorbs routing and paraphrasing load via frontier scale, compact GPT-6-Luna exposes the fragility of end-to-end generative router–ticket hierarchies: DSH-SuperAgent drops to 27.8%27.8\% (C-2 and M-1 at 0.0%0.0\%; hygiene 63.3%63.3\%) as its compact router drops critical arguments during ticket summarization and mis-filters personal app requests. By offloading ingress gating to the lightweight System-1 MMU (TypeSafe Jev) while preserving the original user spine verbatim, ClonAct reaches 48.9%48.9\% (+21.1+21.1 pp, 2222W/33L, p=0.0002p=0.0002) with 100.0%100.0\% hygiene.

Backbone floors vs. universal scheduling invariants. Traces also demarcate the single-task ceiling pθ⋆p_{\theta}^{\star} in Equation 1: Qwen3.8-Flash ends multi-file coding turns early across all arms (27.3%27.3\%–36.4%36.4\% on Bench-60 Coding). On GPT-6-Luna, ClonAct scores 0/60/6 on Bench-60 O-1 while passing 12/1212/12 (100.0%100.0\%) read-only checks, highlighting an extreme instance of post-alignment conservatism on multi-turn office tracks: forensic logs (Appendix F) decompose these six failures into three post-commit write refusals (two of which fail DSH-Mono and DSH-SuperAgent identically) and three single-item near-misses. Across all three backbones (3/33/3), ClonAct consistently leads Combined-90 verifiers, Tier-1 safety (98.5%98.5\%–100.0%100.0\%), Micro-30 hygiene (100.0%100.0\%), H-3 (80.0%80.0\%–100.0%100.0\%), and C-2 over DSH-SuperAgent (+25.0+25.0 to +58.3+58.3 pp).

4.6 Qualitative Trajectory Analysis

Execution traces (Appendix F) show these mechanisms directly. When concurrent requests extend groupby() in Jinja2 with case_sensitive and reverse, DSH-SuperAgent’s blind workers pass local tests yet overwrite the first signature upon merge (TypeError); in ClonAct, a Tier-0 AST alert triggers four peek_peer_cell reads to unify both parameters cleanly. When a foreground brief in Outlines asks for “read-only tracking—do not modify business code” while an external issue implements types.guid, DSH-SuperAgent’s router suppresses all edits, whereas ClonAct isolates the brief in a zero-worktree Observer Cell while the coding cell passes all 8484 tests.

5 Related Work

Multi-Agent Topologies, Agent OS, and Concurrency Control. Collaborative agent systems use role hierarchies, peer chats, and router–worker pipelines (Hong et al., 2024; Wu et al., 2024; Qian et al., 2024; Qiao, 2026; DeepSeek Harness Team, 2026). Toolformer, ReAct, Reflexion, CodeAct, SWE-agent, and OpenHands develop tool use and agent execution methods (Schick et al., 2023; Yao et al., 2023; Shinn et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2024b; Yang et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2025). Separate failure and scaling studies identify coordination failures and task-dependent gains from multi-agent architectures (Cemri et al., 2025; Kim et al., 2025); Anthropic reports deployments where consolidating subagents improved quality and efficiency (Sarkis, 2026). The benefits of role decomposition therefore depend on the task and coordination regime. AIOS (Mei et al., 2025) schedules inference, tools, and storage across agent applications; ClonAct instead multiplexes interleaved user turns within one workspace. HAI-Agent studies handoff interventions (Wang et al., 2026), whereas our in-place promotion avoids prose ticket rewriting. Our isolated execution and trial-merge validation adapt Optimistic Concurrency Control (Kung & Robinson, 1981) to code and workspace reconciliation.

Context Management and KV-Cache Reuse. Memory systems include OS-inspired paging (Packer et al., 2023), skill libraries (Wang et al., 2024a), and long-term memory stores (Xu et al., 2025; Chhikara et al., 2025). Trajectory management spans observation masking (Lindenbauer et al., 2025), information reduction (Xiao et al., 2026), compression (Kang et al., 2026; Zhu et al., 2026; Liu et al., 2026), branching histories (Wu et al., 2025a), and learned memory or folding policies (Yu et al., 2026; Sun et al., 2026). KVCOMM and LRAgent study cache sharing with internal KV access (Ye et al., 2025; Jeon et al., 2026). PagedAttention and SGLang provide serving-level memory and reuse mechanisms (Kwon et al., 2023; Zheng et al., 2024). Our black-box scheduler retains stable prefixes compatible with provider caching; these serving papers do not establish how a commercial API shares cache tensors. We report provider cache-hit telemetry separately from this architectural motivation.

Interactive and Asynchronous Agent Benchmarks. Coding and app benchmarks evaluate task execution (Jimenez et al., 2024; Trivedi et al., 2024; Wu et al., 2025b); other settings emphasize dynamic user interaction (Yao et al., 2025; Vijayvargiya et al., 2025; Raghavendra et al., 2026), asynchronous app events (Froger et al., 2026), mock-tool streaming queues (Qiao, 2026), or paired-agent coding (Khatua et al., 2026). Building upon these substrates, Synaptic-Bench-150, AppWorld-Micro-30, and Synaptic-Stream-60 combine un-partitioned single-window intake, deterministic tool-step Step-Hooks, multi-rate arrival streams, and cross-modal/repository state coupling alongside a zero-coupling control.

6 Conclusion and Limitations

We studied how to coordinate concurrent, always-on personal agents behind a single continuous interface when all dialogue and execution contexts share identical frozen System-2 weights. Controlled comparisons across five kernel-locked paradigms show that linear single-session loops suffer cross-topic bleed and head-of-line stalling, whereas anthropomorphic router–ticket hierarchies introduce lossy handoffs, heavy routing overhead, and blind merges. By scheduling context blocks directly as virtualized resources, ClonAct unifies non-generative ingress multiplexing, in-place align-to-execute promotion, footprint-aware synaptic reconciliation with a portable trial merge gate, and byte-locked prefix retention. Across episodic, streaming, and multi-model evaluations, this separation achieves the trial-merge accuracy ceiling at roughly half the router token footprint, matches top surge-stream completion with zero-timeout observability, and highlights the central principle that homogeneous-weight concurrency is a context-scheduling problem rather than an organizational role-design problem.

Limitations. Three boundaries define immediate directions for future work. First, control-plane generalization and pricing: our cross-backbone evaluation (Table 4) pairs all three System-2 models with a shared lightweight System-1 classifier, and flat uncached System-1 calls can offset System-2 token savings under high event-to-task ratios (such as Surge Stream-60) when cached System-2 prefix reads are deeply discounted; extending same-weight log-probability gating beyond DeepSeek-V4.1, auditing classifier calibration, and batching or prefix-caching System-1 calls remain open optimizations. Second, workspace granularity and cold-start ambiguity: fine-grained symbol tracking currently parses Python ASTs (falling back to file/CLI footprints elsewhere), write cells mount Git worktrees uniformly even for pure app-API writes, and terse pronoun-heavy follow-ups during the initial 11–22 turns before cells accumulate distinct footprints can require explicit disambiguation; multi-language Tree-sitter tracking and modality-gated worktree mounting are direct systems extensions. Third, backbone ceiling and streaming scope: training-free context scheduling remains bounded by the frozen backbone’s undisturbed single-task ceiling pθ⋆p_{\theta}^{\star}, and Synaptic-Stream-60 evaluates S=3S=3 conflict-free streams to isolate queueing dynamics (requiring epoch-versioned prefixes under unbroken load), leaving larger-scale streaming combined with live repository merge conflicts for future evaluation.

Impact Statement

This paper presents work whose goal is to advance the reliability and computational efficiency of concurrent tool-using language model agents by scheduling context blocks directly as virtualized resources. By eliminating redundant natural-language ticket serialization and maintaining stable context prefixes across concurrent tasks, our architecture substantially reduces prompt token expenditure and wall-clock latency while enforcing deterministic read-only and pre-merge safety checks. Deploying always-on personal agents over user repositories, databases, and communication channels carries broader considerations around workspace sandboxing, authorization boundaries, and unintended side effects, which motivate the strict executor-level write gating and isolated trial reconciliation studied in this work.

Appendix A Notation Summary, Complete Scheduling Algorithm, and Proof of Proposition 3.1

To make the main formulation self-contained across Sections 2, 3 and 4, Table 5 summarizes the notation used throughout the paper, Algorithm 1 specifies the full four-stage scheduling and settlement loop of ClonAct, and the proof below verifies each invariant of Proposition 3.1.

Proof of Proposition 3.1.

We verify each guarantee directly from the construction of Algorithm 1:

  1. 1.

    Prefix Byte Identity Within Wave ee: Every cell 𝒞k\mathcal{C}_{k} instantiated or resumed during wave ee constructs its prompt sequence via Equation 2 as T0(e)⊕Sk⊕HkT_{0}^{(e)}\oplus S_{k}\oplus H_{k}, where T0(e)=Pstatic⊕L1⊕L2(e)T_{0}^{(e)}=P_{\mathrm{static}}\oplus L_{1}\oplus L_{2}^{(e)} embeds the identical static instructions, workspace conventions, and full union tool schema UtoolsU_{\mathrm{tools}} regardless of lifecycle state σk\sigma_{k}. Because newly verified L2 contracts enter staging queue QstageQ_{\mathrm{stage}} rather than mutating L2(e)L_{2}^{(e)} mid-wave, and recalled L3 entries append strictly to the right-hand tail of HkH_{k}, the leading byte prefix T0(e)T_{0}^{(e)} remains invariant across all model invocations within wave ee.

  2. 2.

    Executor Tool-API Read-Only Guard: Whenever ContextMMU assigns a turn to σk∈{align,obs}\sigma_{k}\in\{\mathrm{align},\mathrm{obs}\}, no Git worktree is mounted, and the DSH executor plugin guard ℳro\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ro}} (synaptic_worker_plugin) deterministically denies file-write and delegation tool APIs (write, edit, subagent, subagent_fork, send_message, interrupt_agent), while bash is deterministically disabled during non-inspection alignment. (As noted in the Security Scope remark in Section 3, kernel-level zero-mutation protection against arbitrary shell side effects during read-only workspace inspection relies on OS-level read-only filesystem sandboxing such as a read-only macOS Seatbelt profile.)

  3. 3.

    Acyclic Synaptic Termination: Let 𝒢syn=({1,…,Kt},Esyn)\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{syn}}=(\{1,\dots,K_{t}\},E_{\mathrm{syn}}) track milestone delta broadcasts within an episode. Each Tier-1 broadcast from milestone mkm_{k} of 𝒞k\mathcal{C}_{k} to 𝒞j\mathcal{C}_{j} records key (hash(mk),k→j)∈ℛsyn(\mathrm{hash}(m_{k}),k\to j)\in\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{syn}} and marks injected tail notes as non-re-broadcastable observations, eliminating same-milestone echo cycles. Given a bounded per-cell step/milestone budget MmaxM_{\max}, total synaptic deliveries across all cells are strictly bounded by Mmax​Kt​(Kt−1)M_{\max}K_{t}(K_{t}-1) and terminate in finite steps.

  4. 4.

    Single-Task Reduction: When Kt=1K_{t}=1 with a single undisturbed task (s1=chats_{1}=\mathrm{chat}, Φ1∩Φj=∅\Phi_{1}\cap\Phi_{j}=\emptyset), conditioned on single-cell ingress routing, ContextMMU routes directly to 𝒞1\mathcal{C}_{1}, in-place promotion preserves T0(e)⊕S1T_{0}^{(e)}\oplus S_{1} verbatim without intermediate ticket summarization, and Settlement Path A fast-tracks the verified worktree commit onto the main branch with zero auxiliary LLM merge turns, reducing prompt construction and execution to the underlying single-session DSH loop.

Appendix B Multi-Stream Benchmark Construction, Step-Hooks, Verifiers, and Input Samples

Synaptic-Bench-150 (N=150N=150 Episodes, 413413 Deterministic Verifiers). Synaptic-Bench-150 (public release 1.0.0, canonical JSONL SHA-256 6031dd9ddc42d902...ab1dce7b) mounts live multi-environment workspaces combining Git repositories, PostgreSQL/SQLite databases, local document trees, and personal app sandboxes derived from SWE-bench Verified (Chowdhury et al., 2024), SWE-Interact (Raghavendra et al., 2026), Ambig-SWE (Vijayvargiya et al., 2025), CooperBench (Khatua et al., 2026), Gaia2 (Froger et al., 2026), and MCPMark (Wu et al., 2025b). Across 150150 composite episodes (6060 distinct upstream repository/sandbox clusters), every paradigm receives the identical un-pre-partitioned arrival stream mixing foreground chat turns with 150150 external bystander noise messages and duplicate webhook alerts (Table 6).

Deterministic Tool-Count Step-Hooks. Wall-clock timers introduce severe speed confounds across agent architectures: an amendment fired at t=60​st=60\text{s} catches a fast single-session loop after it has already finished editing, while catching a slower router–worker pipeline before its worker even starts. In tracks O-3, C-3, and H-2, our harness intercepts cumulative tool-execution callbacks ctc_{t} at the DSH worker transport layer and fires mid-flight user amendments, requirement refinements, or full goal overturns at exact pre-registered step thresholds ct=τhookc_{t}=\tau_{\mathrm{hook}}, guaranteeing that every paradigm encounters interruptions at an identical stage of execution progress.

Two-Tier External-State Verifier Contract. No LLM-as-a-judge is used for task scoring. Every episode is graded strictly by programmatic state assertions partitioned into two tiers (an episode passes iff all Tier-1 and Tier-2 checks pass):

  • •

    Tier-1 Orchestration Safety (161161 checks on Synaptic-Bench-150): Verifies (i) read-only zero-mutation via pre/post SQLite table hashes and git status --porcelain / commit-SHA equality during alignment and lookup turns, (ii) noise & duplicate hygiene verifying zero side effects from bystander chatter and single-execution idempotency under duplicate webhook bursts, and (iii) clean rollback verifying zero residual edits on aborted/overturned tasks.

  • •

    Tier-2 Task State Oracles (252252 checks on Synaptic-Bench-150): Executes upstream repository pytest suites directly on the canonical main branch (for C-2, running the union test suite of both concurrent features jointly after all merges complete) alongside PostgreSQL, filesystem, and Gaia2 database state assertions.

AppWorld-Micro-30 (N=30N=30) and Synaptic-Stream-60 (33 Streams, 6060 Tasks). AppWorld-Micro-30 (public release 1.0.0, SHA-256 b407b896b58ddee4...7893a761) pairs 6060 atomic errands (2222 read-only lookups and 3838 write errands across Spotify, Gmail, Venmo, Phone, Amazon, Simple Note, and File System) into 3030 strictly app-disjoint episodes (Δ​DBA∩Δ​DBB=∅\Delta\mathrm{DB}_{A}\cap\Delta\mathrm{DB}_{B}=\emptyset) alongside 7070 group-chat noise messages and 3030 duplicate alerts. Synaptic-Stream-60 (release 3.0.0, SHA-256 f6a2f839a71c475f...a5f04459) constructs three conflict-free heterogeneous streams (STREAM_01 and STREAM_02 mounting Click/Jinja2/DSPy monorepos; STREAM_03 mounting Click/DSPy/NetworkX) audited for zero CooperBench-feature or SWE-instance overlap with Bench-150 (including all H-4 waves) and zero AppWorld task-ID or generator-ID overlap with Micro-30. Each stream delivers 240240 chronologically opaque events over streaming channels using 1717 distinct human supervisor identities/emails (zero benchmark category tags, opaque IDs, and live redaction of AppWorld supervisor.Task.instruction to prevent lookahead leakage): 2020 requests (33 strictly disjoint coding features across separate sub-projects with 0%0\% intra-stream file overlap and zero Git merge conflicts by construction, 1111 multi-step AppWorld writes of difficulty 22–33, and 66 read-only lookups), 22 directly tested specification amendments arriving +18​s+18\text{s} after the core request (+7.2​s+7.2\text{s} in Surge, where all arrival timestamps are divided by 2.52.5), 178178 unmentioned group messages across four channels, 2424 colleague reposts (never firing after a task’s amendment), and 1616 untagged status checks (60​s60\text{s} timeout reported as right-censored, mixing natural English and Chinese status-check templates identically across all paradigms). Offline gold verification confirms all 99 coding features fail on the base commit and pass simultaneously on the composed diff while unselected upstream CooperBench suites remain failing, alongside all 5151 AppWorld tasks via unmodified TestTracker (60/6060/60 verified, 00 initial false positives); monotonic-clock snapshots record exact task stabilization timestamps tstable,it_{\mathrm{stable},i} within τ=600​s\tau=600\text{s} per-task deadlines, running each stream in an isolated OS subprocess to prevent cross-run thread contention. Upstream commits and parquet digests are pinned in upstream_lock.json and source_lock.json from official appworld==0.1.3.post1 data.

Appendix C Implementation Specifications, Hyperparameters, Cost Breakdown, and Verbatim Prompts

Execution-Kernel Parity Across All Paradigms. To eliminate low-level scaffolding confounders, every paradigm and ablation arm runs atop the identical Node.js worker runtime (@deepseek-ai/dsh pinned at v0.2.1-rc.3) sharing identical atomic tools (read, write, edit, glob, grep, and 5​s5\text{s} auto-backgrounded bash with job polling), automatic watermark compaction (dsh-compaction-basic), tool-output pruning, macOS Seatbelt (sandbox-exec) isolation, and the identical <workspace_agents_md> workspace conventions block. No external regex pre-filtering is applied to any arm, and billed token telemetry (uncachedInputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens, outputTokens) is extracted uniformly from DSH’s session_projcache SQLite table (summing MMU classifier tokens for ClonAct). The four baselines are instantiated as strong, faithful realizations of their paradigms:

  • •

    DSH-Mono (Single-Session Loop): Runs one persistent DSH session in the primary workspace with subagent tools disabled; mid-flight events arriving during active tool execution inject via DSH’s native steer next-step inbox mechanism.

  • •

    DSH-Subagent-Fork and DSH-Subagent-Neutral (Subagent Delegation Variants): Equips the primary DSH session with dsh-tool-subagent (spawn), dsh-subagent-fork-in-process (inheriting completed KV prefixes), and dsh-tool-subagent-control. DSH-Subagent-Fork uses a Delegation-First system prompt adapted from Qiao (2026), with harness-specific tool names and worktree isolation/merge instructions, whereas DSH-Subagent-Neutral (evaluated on Synaptic-Stream-60) exposes the identical subagent tools under a neutral system prompt to test voluntary delegation.

  • •

    DSH-AgentTeam (Steelman Lead + Blackboard + Peer Mailbox): Pairs a write-gated Team Lead session with on-demand isolated-worktree Teammate sessions sharing (a) an append-only team_board (recording task DAG status, touched files, and findings via tail-injected notices that preserve KV-cache prefixes) and (b) peer-to-peer team_mailbox messaging. Upon completion, if sequential git merge encounters conflict markers, the Lead/Merger is explicitly permitted to inspect team_board and conflict markers to resolve conflicts before testing.

  • •

    DSH-SuperAgent (Official Router–Ticket–Worker Prototype): Runs the unmodified dsh-superagent-prototype repository (DeepSeek Harness Team, 2026, detached commit 8c32a9d), including its native Engine, MasterAssessor, thread-keyed followupOwners pass-through, and isolated DshExecutor worktrees under symmetric channel allowlists (raising maxWorkers to 1616 on Synaptic-Stream-60 to prevent artificial worker-slot throttling under 2020-request streams, and promoting verified worker commits only at quiescent stage/turn boundaries).

Hyperparameters, Runtime Environment, and Dual-Tier Pricing Schedule. Table 8 lists all model wire protocols, MMU thresholds, elastic trunk capacities, runtime timeouts, and official API unit prices used for separate System-2 and System-1 cost accounting across all experiments.

Separate System-2 / System-1 Token, Cache-Hit, and Dual-Tier Cost Decomposition. Because ClonAct pairs stateful System-2 worker contexts (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, benefiting from prefix KV-caching) with stateless single-pass System-1 ingress classifiers (TypeSafe Jev, billed flat at $0.042/1M input and $0 output with no KV cache), pooling both tiers into one cache denominator or pricing System-1 at System-2 uncached rates distorts both metrics. Table 9 therefore reports System-2 cached/uncached/output tokens and System-2 prefix cache hit rate strictly separately from System-1 input tokens, alongside dual-tier USD costs using DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash official off-peak rates ($0.003 hit / $0.15 miss / $0.60 out per 1M) and TypeSafe Jev rates ($0.042/1M input, $0 output). Across all three benchmarks, ClonAct sustains a 96.9%96.9\%–97.9%97.9\% System-2 worker prefix cache hit rate; on Bench-150 (N=150N=150 totals), System-1 ingress uses 2.86​M2.86\text{M} input tokens (0.56%0.56\% of total prompt tokens; 0.20​M0.20\text{M} unbilled structured output tokens excluded from System-2 billing) costing just $0.12 (1.7%1.7\% of total spend), reducing total spend by 38.9%38.9\% vs. DSH-SuperAgent ($6.92 vs. $11.33) and 15.0%15.0\% vs. DSH-AgentTeam ($8.15). On Synaptic-Stream-60, ClonAct cuts System-2 spend by 19.1%19.1\% (Surge: $0.427 vs. $0.528) and 43.5%43.5\% (Moderate: $0.370 vs. $0.655) relative to DSH-SuperAgent, while 301301–303303 stateless Jev calls across 240240 omnichannel events add $0.118–$0.124/stream ($0.0004/call), yielding 24.6%24.6\% lower total Moderate spend ($0.494 vs. $0.655) and near-parity Surge spend ($0.545 vs. $0.528) at 45.1%45.1\% fewer tokens. Finally, in the same-weight log-probability control (ClonAct w/ Logprob-MMU, routing 671/671671/671 System-1 calls via deepseek-chat max_tokens=1, logprobs=True with 00 Jev calls), Bench-60 (N=60N=60) uses 208.4​M208.4\text{M} S2 hit / 4.01​M4.01\text{M} S2 miss / 2.60​M2.60\text{M} S2 out (98.1%98.1\% S2 hit) plus 2.56​M2.56\text{M} S1 logprob prompt tokens (13.0%13.0\% S1 hit) for $3.12 total off-peak USD ($2.79 S2 + $0.34 S1; $0.052/ep), and Micro-30 (N=30N=30) uses 14.91​M14.91\text{M} S2 hit / 0.95​M0.95\text{M} S2 miss / 0.28​M0.28\text{M} S2 out (94.0%94.0\% S2 hit) plus 0.74​M0.74\text{M} S1 tokens for $0.45 total ($0.35 S2 + $0.10 S1; $0.015/ep).

Appendix D Stratified Sampling, IPW Estimation, and Streaming Statistical Inference

Pre-Registered Bench-60 Deterministic Stratification and Horvitz–Thompson IPW. To eliminate cherry-picking bias while bounding multi-model and ablation compute, Bench-60 selects exactly 40.0%40.0\% of each Synaptic-Bench-150 domain (18/4518/45 Office: 66 per track; 22/5522/55 Coding: 55 C-1, 1212 C-2, 55 C-3; 20/5020/50 Hybrid: 66 H-1, 66 H-2, 55 H-3, 33 H-4) solely by sorting episode IDs via deterministic hash SHA-256("PA60-v1:" + episode_id) (preserving the frozen codebase hash salt for exact reproducibility) while maximizing distinct upstream repository/environment cluster coverage (G=33G=33). Because Bench-60 retains all 1010 true-conflict C-2 pairs (πtrue=10/10=1.0\pi_{\mathrm{true}}=10/10=1.0) and samples 22 of 1010 disjoint C-2 pairs (πclean=2/10=0.2\pi_{\mathrm{clean}}=2/10=0.2), whereas other strata use πh=nh/Nh\pi_{h}=n_{h}/N_{h}, we compute the exact unbiased Horvitz–Thompson estimator (Horvitz & Thompson, 1952) over N^=∑i∈Bench-60wi=150.0\hat{N}=\sum_{i\in\text{Bench-60}}w_{i}=150.0 (wi=1/πh⁡(i)w_{i}=1/\pi_{h(i)}), μ^IPW=1150​∑i∈Bench-60yi/πh⁡(i)\widehat{\mu}_{\mathrm{IPW}}=\frac{1}{150}\sum_{i\in\text{Bench-60}}y_{i}/\pi_{h(i)}, with cluster-robust standard errors computed over the G=33G=33 upstream clusters.

Episodic Hypothesis Tests and Continuous-Stream Block & Cluster Inference. Across episodic benchmarks (Bench-150, Bench-60, Micro-30, and Combined-90), binary episode pass-rate comparisons between paired arms on identical episode sets use the exact two-sided McNemar test (McNemar, 1947) (reporting one-sided directional pp-values only on pre-registered single-variable ablation hypotheses where removing a mechanism predicts degradation on its target slice). On Synaptic-Stream-60, tasks within a continuous stream share queueing backlog and repository state, violating naive i.i.d. assumptions. We therefore separate within-stream descriptive tests from cluster-level inference over the S=3S=3 independent streams (implemented deterministically with fixed RNG seed 20261118 and B=20,000B=20{,}000 resamples):

  1. 1.

    Within-Stream Circular Block Bootstrap (95%95\% CI): For each stream s∈{1,2,3}s\in\{1,2,3\} (ns=20n_{s}=20 chronologically ordered tasks), paired capped waiting-time differences ds,i=min⁡(Ws,i(A),τ)−min⁡(Ws,i(B),τ)d_{s,i}=\min(W_{s,i}^{(A)},\tau)-\min(W_{s,i}^{(B)},\tau) are resampled in contiguous circular blocks of width bs=max⁡(2,⌈ns⌉)=5b_{s}=\max(2,\lceil\sqrt{n_{s}}\rceil)=5 (wrapping modulo nsn_{s}) to preserve local queueing autocorrelation, and averaged equally across streams.

  2. 2.

    Hierarchical Stream-Plus-Block Bootstrap (95%95\% CI): First resamples S=3S=3 streams with replacement, then applies circular block resampling (bs=5b_{s}=5) within each sampled stream, targeting the equal-weight mean stream paired difference.

  3. 3.

    Exact Stream-Cluster Sign-Flip Permutation vs. Task-Paired Permutation: The cluster-level permutation evaluates all 2S=82^{S}=8 stream-level sign flips on stream means {d¯1,d¯2,d¯3}\{\bar{d}_{1},\bar{d}_{2},\bar{d}_{3}\}. Because S=3S=3 imposes an exact resolution floor of pmin=2/23=0.25p_{\min}=2/2^{3}=0.25 even when one arm beats another on 3/33/3 streams, we report stream win counts (3/33/3), hierarchical stream-cluster CIs, within-stream block CIs, and descriptive task-paired Monte Carlo sign-flip pp-values (B=20,000B=20{,}000) transparently side by side.

Appendix F Residual Failure Analysis of ClonAct and Forensic Trajectory Walkthroughs

Systematic Residual Error Decomposition of ClonAct. To understand where ClonAct still fails even on the strongest backbone (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017), Table 17 exhaustively decomposes all 38/15038/150 failed episodes on Synaptic-Bench-150 and all failed tasks on Synaptic-Stream-60 (3/603/60 in Surge; 2/602/60 in Moderate). Three diagnostic patterns stand out:

  1. 1.

    Zero Tier-1 Orchestration Failures on Bench-150 (0/380/38): Every single failed ClonAct episode passes all Tier-1 safety, read-only, noise, and rollback checks (161/161=100.0%161/161=100.0\%); all 3838 failures stem from Tier-2 task-solve verifiers. Moreover, 20/3820/38 (52.6%52.6\%) are shared backbone-ceiling failures where all five paradigms fail on the exact same episode (99 Coding, 66 Hybrid, 55 Office), directly reflecting the single-task ceiling pθ⋆p_{\theta}^{\star} in Equation 1. Only 18/15018/150 (12.0%12.0\%) represent ClonAct-specific residual errors where at least one baseline succeeds (55 Coding, 55 Hybrid, 88 Office), most commonly from conservative multi-turn clarification under-execution in Office tracks (O-1, O-3) or partial edge-case patches.

  2. 2.

    Near-Ceiling Conflict-Free Surge Reliability (3/603/60 failed, 00 regressions): Under 2.5×2.5\times Surge, ClonAct completes 20/2020/20 (100.0%100.0\%) on S-1 and 57/6057/60 (95.0%95.0\%) overall with zero test regressions (0/00/0). Its three residual errors consist of one Click feature patch missing batch_size parameter forwarding (STREAM_02_T01, 12/17312/173 tests failing), one multi-step AppWorld write reaching 80.0%80.0\% partial assertion pass (STREAM_02_T14, acct_08), and one read-only lookup (STREAM_03_T09, acct_14) unverified within τ=600​s\tau=600\text{s}.

  3. 3.

    Near-Ceiling Moderate Reliability (2/602/60 failed, 22 recovered regressions): Under Moderate arrivals, ClonAct reaches 20/2020/20 on both S-1 and S-3 (58/60=96.7%58/60=96.7\% overall) with 100.0%100.0\% (18/1818/18) read-only QA accuracy. Its two failures mirror the same two S-2 tasks: STREAM_02_T01 missing a single exception-type assertion (1/1731/173 tests failing, raising ValueError instead of expected TypeError) and STREAM_02_T14 reaching 60.0%60.0\% partial assertion pass.

Targeted Forensic Audits: C-2 Disjoint Control and GPT-6-Luna O-1. Two specific slices where a baseline exceeds ClonAct merit transparent episode-level decomposition from the saved execution logs:
